assessments.reasoning: The execution reference supplies the visibility rule, the effect of an enclosing global declaration, and the compile-time failure for a missing function binding. The added span explains how the whole function body determines local status before an assignment executes. The annotation-scope discussion bounds the inference for class namespaces and type parameters. Together with the statement reference, this supports the ordinary-function claim for the enrolled 3.13.0 edition. The special __class__ mechanism remains outside this finding.

The statement reference identifies enclosing functions as the scopes that can supply a binding. It selects the closest binding when several qualify and specifies SyntaxError when none qualifies. The execution reference supplies the compile-time timing and explains lexical availability. I opened the retained original material for both chapters and verified their full-body and candidate-span digests.

challenge.method: Compare a farther function local hidden by an intervening global declaration with a visible outer local whose assignment has yet to execute. Also check whether a module binding, ordinary class attribute, or type parameter could rescue an otherwise invalid declaration. Compare an intervening function with no binding against one with its own local binding. Check whether an earlier use in the declaring function creates a separate failure.
challenge.results: The global directive redirects resolution and can leave the declaration without an eligible function local. A pending assignment can already determine lexical eligibility. Module bindings and ordinary class attributes cannot supply the required local, and the reference explicitly excludes rebinding a type parameter. An empty intervening scope leaves the farther binding eligible. An intervening local binding takes precedence. Earlier use or assignment in the declaring scope can independently cause SyntaxError, which the claim's syntax condition excludes.

limitations: The name `__class__` is excluded because Python’s Data model describes an implicit class closure reference.
An intervening function’s global declaration can make a farther function-local binding unavailable. Module globals and ordinary class attributes do not supply function-local bindings.
The lexical binding rule does not require the variable already to have a runtime value when the declaration is parsed.
The execution controls used CPython 3.13.5. The claim is about the exact pinned Python 3.13.0 reference.
The two cited chapters have the same documentation lineage.
This review reopened retained source bytes. Historical reproduction results remain separate.
